body: # Meta slams Australia’s bid to make tech giants pay for sharing news articles. Meta faces a compulsory levy that will amount to 2.25% of their Australian revenue. Tech giant Meta has attacked Australia’s “grossly unfair” bid to make social media companies pay for news, saying it is vehemently opposed to the draft laws. and Instagram, said in a statement: “Our position is clear: this law is poorly designed, grossly unfair, and will fail to deliver a diverse and sustainable news industry. Social media companies including Meta, Google and TikTok will first be given a chance to strike content deals with local news publishers. If they refuse, they face a compulsory levy that will amount to 2.25% of their Australian revenue. When Canberra mooted similar laws in 2024, Meta announced that Australian users would no longer be able to access the “news” tab. Australia’s University of Canberra has found that more than half the country uses social media as a source of news.

# ‘Grossly unfair’: Meta slams Australia’s bid to make platforms pay for news. *Facebook parent company says proposals violate Australia’s commitments under its free trade agreement with the US.*. Social media giant Meta has hit out at Australia’s latest plans to force digital platforms to support media outlets financially, labelling the proposals “poorly designed” and “grossly unfair.”. Meta, the parent company of Facebook, WhatsApp and Instagram, said on Thursday that the government’s News Bargaining Incentive (NBI) would shield news publishers from needing to undertake the innovation necessary for a sustainable media landscape. Meta also said the “economically incoherent” proposals would not lead to a sustainable news sector and “plainly” violate Australia’s commitments under its free trade agreement with the United States. Under the centre-left Labor Party government’s plans, social media and search platforms would face a 2.25 percent levy on Australian revenues if they do not make deals to pay Australian outlets for their news content.

## Firstpost's Post. ### **Firstpost**. Meta Warns Australia's Tech Tax Could Trigger Trade Dispute. Meta has accused Australia of violating its free trade agreement with the United States over a proposed levy on major technology firms that do not sign licensing deals with local media outlets.
